description: Check what became of a previously submitted request — no sign-in needed, guests welcome. Use when the customer asks whether the notary confirmed, moved, cancelled, or merged it. Accepts: `reference` — the id returned at submission or the token from the emailed confirm link. Returns the service plus status and timing (PII-minimal — never address, name, or notes; Pacific time, e.g. scheduledAtPacific). Fails if the reference is wrong — a not found reply.

reference.description:
The reference id returned when the request was submitted (also accepts
the token from the emailed confirm link).

name: check_request_status

outputSchema.description: PII-minimal status of a request — never the address, name or notes.

displayStatus.description: The customer-facing word: {code, tone}. Code is the derived display status (Signed | Apostilled | ReadyToShip | Shipped | Complete | PartiallyComplete | DealDone | …); tone is ok | warn | err | info | neutral. Quote the code's meaning from `note`, never the stored status.

mergedInto.description: Only for MergedWithOther: the surviving appointment's status and time.

requestedTime.description: Unix seconds the customer asked for on a lead, or null.

service.description: office | apostille | mobile | loan | ron | apostille_mail; null on a legacy row.

status.description: Pending | Scheduled | EnRoute | InProgress | Completed | Notarized | PickedUp | Cancelled | NoShow | MergedWithOther. The STORED operator lifecycle — `Completed` means the notarial act happened (signed), not that the order is done. `note` says what the word means for the customer; read that rather than branching on this.
